This structure allows soil to absorb and retain water more effectively, leading to improved moisture levels for plants. For instance, soil that contains 4-5% organic matter can absorb 4-6 inches of rain per hour, while soil with only about 2% organic matter absorbs significantly less, leading to potential runoff and erosion.

This not only benefits crop health by providing consistent moisture but also helps prevent issues related to flooding and erosion.

Healthy soil acts as a sponge, holding water and gradually releasing it to plants. This is essential for maintaining crop health, especially in periods of drought. Soils rich in organic matter have greater moisture-holding capacity, reducing the need for irrigation and increasing resilience to drought conditions.
